runbook.real-role-denial: Procedure: In a disposable PostgreSQL 17 fixture, create the two harness roles (fitnest_foundation_runtime as a non-owner, no BYPASSRLS, and fitnest_foundation_migrator), apply supabase/migrations/202611010001_foundation.sql, then connect as fitnest_foundation_runtime and attempt: (a) SELECT with app.tenant_id unset; (b) set app.tenant_id to tenant A and read tenant B rows; (c) UPDATE or DELETE on append-only settings_versions/frozen_days/audit; (d) TRUNCATE any table; (e) connect with anon/authenticated and read any fitnest_foundation table. Expected: (a) no rows because RLS fails closed on a NULL tenant; (b) cross-tenant rows are invisible; (c,d) insufficient_privilege; (e) permission denied; PUBLIC is revoked and only fitnest_foundation_runtime holds grants. Diagnose failure: run SELECT current_user, session_user, current_setting('app.tenant_id', true) and inspect information_schema.role_table_grants and pg_policies; a cross-tenant row returned, a successful UPDATE, or any PUBLIC grant indicates a misconfigured RLS policy or GRANT.
runbook.settings-concurrency: Procedure: Build createFoundation over a real pg pool and an authenticate returning server facts, then drive two concurrent postSettings requests for the same tenant/key that both expect the current version, plus one with a stale expectedVersion, and submit two requests reusing one idempotencyKey with different values. Expected: the head read uses SELECT ... FOR UPDATE on settings_heads, so exactly one writer advances to the next version and the loser returns 409 CONFLICT; settings_versions keeps an append-only 1..N history; a reused idempotencyKey with a different payloadHash conflicts; a freeze of the same consumption_day yields one immutable snapshot. Diagnose failure: inspect settings_versions/settings_heads/frozen_days rows and response codes; two heads at the same version, a missing CONFLICT, or a double-inserted snapshot indicates a broken FOR UPDATE, a lost expectedVersion check, or a missing advisory lock.
runbook.migration-reproducibility: Procedure: Reproduce the migration() decision in packages/core/src/foundation/runtime.mjs by passing canonical and applied as the exact same ordered list with nullableMatches=true, backwardCompatible=true, restoreVerified=true, erasuresReplayed=true and a disposable environment, then flip each flag false and set a production/staging environment. Expected: localAllowed is true only when canonical equals applied exactly and every flag is true in a disposable environment; productionAllowed is always false because this library never executes a production migration. Diagnose failure: any canonical/applied mismatch, a destructive or relabeling change, or an untested isolated restore yields localAllowed=false; cross-check docs/delivery/evidence/baseline-migration-review-20261026.json (productionReplayPerformed=false, nullable-plan migration absent from remote history, observedPlanNameNullable=NO).
runbook.casablanca-time: Procedure: Run the pinned Node 24.19.0 + Vitest 5.0.5 suite pnpm test:core, which executes packages/core/src/time/time.test.ts against businessDate/businessIsoWeek, and additionally call businessDate for '2026-10-18T22:59:59.999Z' versus '2026-10-18T23:00:00.000Z', midnight, a phone-timezone offset, and Ramadan/DST transitions, asserting half-open [start,end) intervals. Expected: Africa/Casablanca business date; ISO-week key with startInclusive/endExclusive computed without adding seven 24-hour periods, so Ramadan/transition weeks yield 167/169-hour boundaries; invalid Dates throw RangeError and the passed instant is not mutated. Diagnose failure: a date-label mismatch across UTC offset, a gap or overlap where previous.endExclusive != next.startInclusive, or a 168-hour assumption producing wrong boundaries indicates a broken D-058 mapping.
runbook.worker-retry: Procedure: Exercise the createFoundation worker ports claim/settle/reconcile against a real pool: insert a pending outbox row, claim it (bounded lease <=1h, FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED), settle 'delivered' for two distinct recipients, settle the same recipient again, settle 'failed', settle 'ambiguous' then reconcile providerState delivered/absent, and claim with an expired lease. Expected: at-least-once delivery with unique consumer_receipts/effects; a duplicate settle returns 'replay'; 'failed' clears the lease so the row is re-claimable; 'ambiguous' requires reconcile; reconcile 'absent' releases to failed; a delivered row is never reopened for another worker or a non-delivered outcome. Diagnose failure: a duplicate consumer_effects row, a second effect from an ambiguous outcome, or a delivered row accepting a failure means the outbox/reconcile guards are broken; inspect outbox.state/lease and consumer_effects rows.
runbook.runtime-build: Procedure: Run node tooling/foundation/build-public.mjs --out=/tmp/SAFE_DIRECTORY (which rejects any non-/tmp path) and inspect foundation.mjs, time.mjs, public-config.json and manifest.json. Expected: foundation.mjs rewrites the time import to ./time.mjs; time.mjs is the D-058 module with TypeScript types stripped; public-config.json carries only NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL and NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY with no service-role or database secret; manifest.json recomputes lockfileSha256, workspaceDigest and per-file SHA-256 with revision=null. Diagnose failure: a non-/tmp out path exits 1; a missing time-import rewrite exits 1; any service-role/database URL in public-config.json or a file hash that fails to recompute means the builder leaked a secret or emitted a non-deterministic artifact.

residualRisks: No live application database role or migration role has been observed (runtime-role-config.json: liveConnectionRoleObserved=false, only an inferred postgres pooler username); current_user/session_user and role memberships must be observed through a real application connection outside this baseline (T006).

Role and RLS denial guarantees exist only as schema and code design; they must be exercised against the protected native PostgreSQL 17 suite with real roles and direct Supabase interfaces, not mocks, which is outside this baseline.

Production migration replay was not performed (baseline-migration-review-20261026.json: productionReplayPerformed=false, nullable-plan migration absent from remote history, observedPlanNameNullable=NO); G-T013 founder arbitration with a concrete diff, privileges, data impact and restore procedure remains required.
Settings/freeze concurrency and idempotency are validated only as code plus schema design; concurrent-transaction behavior must be proven against a real PostgreSQL fixture outside this baseline.

Worker outbox at-least-once delivery, bounded retries and provider-outcome reconciliation are not exercised against a real outbox/provider, and no fire-and-forget proof for a request handler is established here.
Casablanca time is a pure prototype; native (Expo 51 / React Native 0.74.5) rendering and device-timezone qualification remain separate downstream obligations not covered by this baseline.
G-SESSION session lifetimes, revocation and refresh-replay policy, and provider refresh exceptions remain downstream of SEC-C and are not certified by this baseline.

Exact dependency pinning is not observed: apps/web/package.json declares numerous 'latest' version specifiers and no lockfile hash is recorded; mandatory CI, artifact-to-commit traceability and demonstrated rollback remain unresolved SEC-32 requirements.
The native mobile directory is absent from the root pnpm workspace; adding it requires separate dependency resolution and a device build, not a YAML edit.

No live deployment is confirmed (runtime-inventory.json: liveDeploymentConfirmed=false) and channel protections for actions/rpc/exports/realtime are recorded as 'unknown'; real Data API/HTTP/realtime authorization must be verified outside this baseline.
T012 identity/referral/wallet scaffolding remains incomplete; no ledger representation or unit scale is established in this baseline.
Local Auth qualification (T003) is prepared but not claimed passed because Docker is absent in the editing environment; the CI result must be read before closing T003.
